fact_text: Shareholders' equity, also called owners' equity, book value or capital, is what remains after a company's liabilities are subtracted from its assets.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Book value per share is total shareholders' equity divided by the total number of shares outstanding, giving the per-share value of the company's net assets on its books.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Price-to-book is the share price divided by book value per share; a result below 1 means the stock trades under its book value, which the analyst treats as a sign of possible undervaluation.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: The analyst says market prices follow demand and supply, so a share can trade well above or well below its book value; book value is the baseline for judging that gap.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Book value growth is the change in book value per share from the prior year, divided by the prior-year figure and multiplied by 100 to give a percentage.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Expected book value is a forecast for the coming year, built by analysts from expected business performance; the analyst applies the same growth formula using forecast earnings per share.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Return on equity is net profit divided by average shareholders' equity, showing the return owners earn on the money they have put into the company.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Return on assets is net profit divided by total assets, showing how much profit the company generates from its asset base.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Equity-to-assets is average shareholders' equity divided by total assets, showing what share of the asset base is funded by owners rather than by borrowed money.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Return on capital employed is EBIT (earnings before interest and taxes) divided by capital employed, where capital employed is average shareholders' equity plus long-term debt or liabilities.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Analysts differ on which debt goes into capital employed: some use only long-term debt, some long-term liabilities, some total debt; the analyst himself uses long-term liabilities.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: The analyst says ROE ignores borrowed money while ROCE includes it, so ROE alone can mislead for a company partly funded by bank loans and ROCE shows the return on all capital used.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Retention ratio is net profit less dividends, divided by net profit and multiplied by 100; per share it can be computed as earnings per share less dividend per share, divided by earnings per share.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Preferred shareholders are paid before ordinary shareholders, so their entitlement is deducted from net profit before per-share ratios; the analyst's simplified calculations leave this out.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: The analyst applies the same formulas to forecast profit to estimate expected ROE, expected retention ratio and expected price-to-book for the coming year, rather than relying only on past results.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Illustration: if a company's land, buildings and machinery would cost 15 lakh to rebuild but its whole listed equity trades for 1 lakh, the analyst says book value reveals the price gap.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Snapshot  Equity Ratios Explained | Book Value, P/B, ROE, ROA, ROCE| PART 03 | Afaque Manzar' (YouTube, 2026-02-14)

fact_text: Illustration: a company with 10 lakh of assets, 7 lakh funded by owners and 3 lakh by a bank loan has 70% equity-to-assets, and the bank-funded assets may be pledged to the lender.
